items.title: Privacy egress monitor
items.summary: Live tracking of what certified/legitimate apps actually send — moving CounterSpy from 'is this spyware?' to 'this app is trusted, but here's what it's exfiltrating; do you consent?'. A per-process egress observer (destination/volume tracking, consent deltas). v1 (now in development): a live TUI 'egress top' via sudo-CLI observation (nettop + lsof), observe-only. Rationale: the v0.3.0 feedback loop measures false positives among flagged apps; the next risk surface is the apps NOT flagged — notarized/allowlisted software that over-collects. Rhymes with the egress-only invariant: watch egress because egress is where the risk lives.

items.title: Phase 1 — Passive reveal: destination names + cleartext extraction
items.summary: First phase of the outbound-visibility program (see docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-14-outbound-traffic-visibility-design.md). Passive DNS-response capture (port 53) builds an IP->hostname cache so the egress tree/zoom/inspect show the name an app actually resolved instead of a bare cloud IP; and the on-demand inspector gains maximal cleartext extraction (structured HTTP request/response, headers, path, body preview) beyond today's text-or-hexdump. No decryption. Reuses a filter-parameterized /dev/bpf capture shared with the per-flow inspector. Names are display-only this phase (raw-IP concern scoring deferred). Foundation for Phases 2-3.

items.title: Phase 2 — TLS key-log decryption (SSLKEYLOGFILE)
items.summary: Capture the TLS session secrets that apps export via SSLKEYLOGFILE (browsers, curl, Go/OpenSSL/NSS tools) and decrypt those flows from the Phase-1 pcap. No trust anchor, no MITM, no traffic modification. Coverage is bounded to apps launched with the key-log env set, and honest about the rest (still shown 'encrypted'). Layers a key-log reader + record decryptor onto the Phase-1 capture substrate.

items.title: Phase 3 — Transparent proxy: decrypt, redact, block
items.summary: Final phase: a local transparent intercepting proxy using a user-installed, reversible root CA -> broad TLS decryption of already-running apps' outbound HTTPS, PLUS active control: redact sensitive fields from outbound payloads and/or block transmissions outright. This is a deliberate, user-driven capability on the user's own hardware, gated behind explicit per-run consent; it is the one phase that crosses CounterSpy's observe-only network invariant (adds active egress control / DLP). Engineering rails: auditable + reversible CA install as features, never corrupt traffic, fail-mode chosen explicitly. Sequenced last so the passive-visibility foundation ships first.

items.title: Sign + notarize the release binaries
items.summary: Add Apple Developer ID codesigning + notarytool notarization to the GoReleaser release pipeline so prebuilt binaries run without any Gatekeeper friction. The v0.4.x release tooling ships UNSIGNED first (curl|sh and Homebrew avoid the quarantine flag; a browser-downloaded tar.gz needs xattr -d com.apple.quarantine); the intent is to wire signing imminently once a Developer ID cert + notarization secrets are in CI. Important for a security tool that runs under sudo — users rightly distrust an unsigned binary. The pipeline is structured so signing is a drop-in step.
